raw_response:
I've been farming these same 10 mu for 40 years, since I was a young bride of 22. Never spent a single day in school — I can barely sign my own name. My husband is 65 now, working odd jobs at a construction site in the county town. It's just the two of us at home, and his back is worse than mine, so most days I'm the one in the field. We need cash for my blood pressure medicine and for when things go wrong, so I watch every yuan. I don't trust those new seeds and fancy methods from the shop. I do what I've always done, and what my neighbors do.

For the wheat, I plant around October 12th, after National Day when the weather cools down. I save my own red-grain seed — two sacks per mu, about 20 jin [10 kg]. Before sowing, I spread half a bag of compound fertilizer per mu and about 20 jin of urea. My nephew read the bag for me — it says 15-something-something, but I just know it's the black-granule one. In March when the wheat turns green, I topdress another 30 jin of urea. My sister-in-law said she cut back to 25 jin this year because prices went up, but last time I did that the wheat turned yellow and I lost sleep over it. Better to use 30 jin and be safe. I water three times: once before winter if there's no rain, once at jointing when the stems shoot up, and once at heading when the ears come out. The pump meter runs fast — costs over 30 yuan each time. I can't afford more.

Maize goes in the day after the combine cuts the wheat, around June 15th. The window is terribly tight — sometimes less than a week. If you miss it, the yield drops and everyone in the village talks about it. I buy hybrid seed from the shop, 4 jin [2 kg] per mu, costs about 80 yuan. I put down half a bag of compound and 25 jin [12.5 kg] of urea per mu at planting. By July I'm busy drying wheat and looking after my courtyard vegetables, so I don't have time or strength to topdress the maize. The summer rain usually helps. I water once, maybe twice if July is dry like last year.

Weeds are bad in both seasons. I spray herbicide once for each crop with my backpack sprayer — costs about 25 yuan per mu. For harvest I hire the combine for wheat. For maize planting I sometimes pay my nephew 100 yuan a day to run the tractor when my husband isn't home and the window is tight. I expect about 900 jin [450 kg] of wheat per mu and 1,000 jin [500 kg] of maize if the weather is kind. All together I'll spend around 4,500 yuan on inputs this year. I wanted to buy more fertilizer but the shop raised prices again, and I need cash in the cabinet. You never know what will happen.
